5788               	; 			' THE BALL IS ON THE GROUND WHEN HE GETS TO IT.
5789               	; 			'
5790               	; 			' The bounce phase used to be `lx AND 31` -- a byte out of
5791               	; 			' the placement table, which is to say arbitrary. Run onto
5792               	; 			' a screen and the first ball might be at the bottom of its
5793               	; 			' arc, where a jump clears it, or at the top, where it has
5794               	; 			' to be ducked, and nothing on the way in told you which.
5795               	; 			' Sometimes you could keep running and jump it; sometimes
5796               	; 			' the same approach at the same speed could not be jumped
5797               	; 			' at all. That is not difficulty, it is a coin toss.
5798               	; 			'
5799               	; 			' So the phase is worked BACKWARDS from the meeting. He
5800               	; 			' closes 4 px a pass and the ball 2, so they meet in
5801               	; 			' (gap / 6) passes; the phase advances one a pass and wraps
5802               	; 			' at 32, so seeding it with the NEGATIVE of that lands it on
5803               	; 			' phase 0 -- the ground -- exactly as they arrive.
5804               	; 			'
5805               	; 			' The gap is the same either way round: he enters at one
5806               	; 			' wall and the ball starts `stag` in from the other, so it
5807               	; 			' is 232 - stag whichever direction the floor runs.
5808               	; 			'
5809               	; 			' It stays forgiving rather than exact. The arc is flat near
5810               	; 			' the bottom, so anything within eight passes either side is
5811               	; 			' still under the jump; and it only holds for an unbroken
5812               	; 			' run, which is the case the player is entitled to read off
5813               	; 			' the screen. Duck, stop or take a hit and everything after
5814               	; 			' is out of step again -- which is the game.
5815               	; 			' obp is a BALL-only field: upd_obst reads it under an
5816               	; 			' IF uk = OB_BALL and nothing else touches it, and every
5817               	; 			' ball has it computed below. It was seeded here from a
5818               	; 			' table byte that no longer exists, and for anything but
5819               	; 			' a ball that seed was never read.
5820               	; 			IF lk = OB_BALL THEN

     BE2E 21F4

6786               	; 		' HE IS STANDING ON A STEP, so he moves at the STEP's rate: 2 px
6787               	; 		' across and 1 up PER PASS -- the staircase's own slope, and exactly
6788               	; 		' what one phase of esc_tick moves the pattern by.
6789               	; 		'
6790               	; 		' NOT `fdv`, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. Everything else in this loop
6791               	; 		' is paced by the frame delta, and pacing him that way too made him
6792               	; 		' outrun the steps the moment a pass cost more than one frame: his
6793               	; 		' feet started planted on a tread and ended floating above it.
6794               	; 		' Pacing the ANIMATION by fdv instead is worse -- four phases cannot
6795               	; 		' be stepped by 2 or 3 without aliasing, and the staircase runs
6796               	; 		' backwards (see esc_tick). The only arrangement that cannot drift
6797               	; 		' is the one where both are driven by the same fixed step, so the
6798               	; 		' rider is clocked by the pass, like the steps he is standing on.
6799               	; 		'
6800               	; 		' THE FIRST FEW PASSES ARE THE STEP ON. Walking on, his feet are on
6801               	; 		' the floor and the bottom tread is 4 to 7 px above them, so he
6802               	; 		' climbs at 2 px a pass until he catches it (the tread is rising at
6803               	; 		' 1, so the gap closes at 1 a pass) and then rides with it. Jumping
6804               	; 		' on he lands ON a tread, so eson is 0 and this never runs.

7339               	; 		' THE FIRST STEP OFF THE MARK IS ALWAYS HEARD. sfw is a distance --
7340               	; 		' a step every fifteen pixels -- so a short tap of the stick moved
7341               	; 		' him a few pixels and made NO sound at all. That does not read as
7342               	; 		' a short step, it reads as the controls being ignored, and it is
7343               	; 		' worst exactly where a player taps rather than holds: lining up a
7344               	; 		' jump, or edging around a hazard.
7345               	; 		'
7346               	; 		' Priming the accumulator to the threshold makes the very next pass
7347               	; 		' fire. It does not cheat the RATE: the trigger subtracts fifteen
7348               	; 		' rather than zeroing, so the pixels actually travelled still carry
7349               	; 		' into the following step and a held run comes out at 6.9 a second

8265               	;
8266               	; 	' THE VICTROLA, AS CHARACTERS. It never moves, so a sprite spent a
8267               	; 	' scan-line slot on something that can be painted once when the screen is
8268               	; 	' drawn -- and at one 16x16 sprite it could only ever be one colour and
8269               	; 	' one size. Four cells is twice the area for no sprite at all.
8270               	; 	'
8271               	; 	' It stands ON the slab, so it fills the band's rows 2 and 3; row 4 is
8272               	; 	' the floor bar itself -- and a PRIZE uses those same two rows.
8273               	; 	'
8274               	; 	' THEY CAN SHARE A BAND, AND THE CLAIM THAT USED TO BE HERE WAS WRONG.
8275               	; 	' It said the two never share a screen because "genstore keeps prizes off
8276               	; 	' the screens that carry hazards". That stopped being true the moment
8277               	; 	' hazard placement moved into the per-Krook stor_lvl table, and nothing
8278               	; 	' noticed, because the prize table is not part of the level table and
8279               	; 	' every check was written about one object at a time. Two money bags ended
8280               	; 	' up standing on a radio -- not fighting it, since the two routines poke
8281               	; 	' different cells and the later writer simply wins, so they read as one
8282               	; 	' merged object.
8283               	; 	'
8284               	; 	' WHAT KEEPS THEM APART IS COLUMNS. A radio stands at column 7, 15 or 23
8285               	; 	' (see lrc below); genstore's _off_the_rack nudges a prize clear of all
8286               	; 	' three, and checklevels.py reads that arithmetic back out of THIS file
8287               	; 	' and fails the build on any overlap.
8288               	; 	'
8289               	; 	' rdall = 1 paints all four cells, 0 repaints only the top-right one --
8290               	; 	' the pulse. Same address arithmetic either way, so the two cannot drift.
8291               	; 	' A BEAM TOP HANGS OUT OF THE FLOOR ABOVE, and the beam it belongs to has
8292               	; 	' just been taken away. `beam_tops` stamps SLABP -- the floor bar with the
8293               	; 	' support carried up through its lower three pixel rows -- into the slab
8294               	; 	' row above every pillar, and it runs BEFORE the radios and prizes are
8295               	; 	' placed. Clearing a pillar's own cells therefore left three grey pixels
8296               	; 	' dangling from the ceiling with nothing under them.
8297               	; 	'
8298               	; 	' TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: only SLABP is put back to SLAB. The row above the
8299               	; 	' top shopping floor is the ROOF DECK, a different character altogether,
8300               	; 	' and writing a floor bar over it would punch a hole in the roof.
8301               	; 	' A SHELF RUN IS FIVE CELLS WIDE and a radio covers two, so one standing
8302               	; 	' on a counter punched a hole through its middle and left the ends either
8303               	; 	' side -- the same incoherence the dangling pillar had, and worse, because
8304               	; 	' a counter reads as one object. The whole unit goes: walk outward along
8305               	; 	' the band's row 2 while the cell is still a shelf top, clearing it and
8306               	; 	' its bottom half together.
8307               	; 	'
8308               	; 	' Bounded at eight steps. The runs are five, so eight is slack rather
8309               	; 	' than a guess -- and an unbounded walk would run off the end of the row
8310               	; 	' if the name table ever held something unexpected.
8311               	; 	#if NES
8312               	; 	' WHAT THE TEMPLATE PUT IN THIS CELL, for a target that cannot read its
8313               	; 	' own video memory back. #nta is the offset INSIDE the band (0-159) and
8314               	; 	' nbl is the band; the answer is the byte SCREEN blitted there.
8315               	; 	'
8316               	; 	' This is the same arithmetic the blit itself does in draw_band --
8317               	; 	' template id out of stor_ix for (band, screen), times 160, plus the
8318               	; 	' offset -- so the two cannot disagree about what is on screen. It is
8319               	; 	' reading what the cell MEANS, not guessing from where the cell is: a
8320               	; 	' coordinate is a fact about this layout, the character is a fact about
8321               	; 	' the world, and only the second is safe to erase on.
8322               	; nes_tpl:
8323               	; 	nti = lv8(nbl)
8324               	; 	nti = nti + klsc
8325               	; 	#ntb = #stix + nti
8326               	; 	ntd = PEEK(#ntb)
8327               	; 	#ntc = #tsrc(ntd)
8328               	; 	#ntc = #ntc + #nta
8329               	; 	#ntc = #ntc + #sttp
8330               	; 	ntv = PEEK(#ntc)
8331               	; 	RETURN
8332               	; 	#endif
8333               	;

9057               	; upd_obst:

9059               	; 	' ONE ACCUMULATOR PER KIND, NOT PER SLOT. Every hazard of a kind moves at
9060               	; 	' that kind's speed, so three calls a pass serve all eight slots.
9061               	; 	'
9062               	; 	' Per-slot would have meant up to eight calls of O(fdv) work every pass --
9063               	; 	' the positive feedback loop CLAUDE.md 3A warns about, where a slow pass is
9064               	; 	' made slower by the very code meant to take the loop rate out of the
9065               	; 	' game's behaviour. It also saves the eight bytes an obacc() would cost,
9066               	; 	' and ColecoVision RAM is the tighter budget.
9067               	; 	pacc = oacb

     D52C 20D2

9358               	; 	' ONE STEP OF A FRACTIONAL SPEED, FOR WHOEVER IS MOVING.
9359               	; 	'
9360               	; 	' `pacc` in and out, `psp64` in (sixty-fourths of a pixel per FRAME),
9361               	; 	' `pspd` out (whole pixels this pass). CVBasic has no locals, so the caller
9362               	; 	' stages its own accumulator in and takes it back out; that costs four
9363               	; 	' statements against the fourteen this used to be, written out per actor.
9364               	; 	'
9365               	; 	' Harry had the only copy. Kelly, the hazards and the bounce phase all need
9366               	; 	' the same thing -- everything the round clock judges has to advance by
9367               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAMES, or the loop rate becomes a difficulty dial and where the
9368               	; 	' player stands decides the outcome (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9369               	; 	'
9370               	; 	' TWO DRAINS CAP THE STEP AT 2 PER FRAME whatever psp64 says (CLAUDE.md
9371               	; 	' 3A: N drains cap the speed at N, and the surplus leaks into a byte that
9372               	; 	' wraps). Every caller is under that: Kelly 102/64 = 1.6, the fastest
9373               	; 	' hazard 76/64 = 1.2, Harry 57/64 = 0.9, the bounce phase 25/64 = 0.4.
9374               	; 	'
9375               	; 	' FIVE FRAMES, AND THREE WAS TOO FEW. At 2 px a frame five frames is 10 px,
9376               	; 	' and to skip a position window an actor must start outside it on one side
9377               	; 	' and land outside on the other, which needs 12. Three was the original bug
9378               	; 	' in miniature: the lift screen runs at almost exactly 20 passes a second,
9379               	; 	' which IS fdv = 3, so every hitch there lost a frame. The clamp exists for
9380               	; 	' a genuine stall and at five it only fires for one.

9869               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9870               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9871               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9872               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9873               	; 	' runs every pass.
9874               	; 	'
9875               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9876               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9877               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9878               	; 	'
9879               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9880               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9881               	; 	'
9882               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9883               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9884               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9885               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9886               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9887               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9888               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9889               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9890               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9891               	; 	'
9892               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9893               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9894               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9895               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9896               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a
9897               	; 	' speed ratio of 2.0 leaves the on-foot chase 0.2 s of slack, which is no
9898               	; 	' chase at all. checkchase.py holds the line.
9899               	; 	' STILL RUNNING FROM THE STAIRS -- and this has to come BEFORE the move,
9900               	; 	' not after it. It sat below the two `IF hmv` blocks, where all it could
9901               	; 	' still reach was the animation counter: he faced the right way, played
9902               	; 	' the run cycle and did not travel a pixel. He stood at the foot of the
9903               	; 	' flight looking busy.
9904               	; 	'
9905               	; 	' TWO THINGS END THE RUN, AND BOTH ARE VISIBLE ON SCREEN.
9906               	; 	'
9907               	; 	' THE KOP ARRIVING ON THIS FLOOR OUTRANKS IT. This used to override the

10000               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
10001               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
10002               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
10003               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
10004               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
10005               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
10006               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
10007               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
10008               	; 	'
10009               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
10010               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
10011               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
10012               	; 	'
10013               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
10014               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
10015               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
10016               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
10017               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
10018               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
10019               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
10020               	; 	'
10021               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
10022               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
10023               	; 	'
10024               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
10025               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
10026               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
10027               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
10028               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
10029               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
10030               	; 	'
10031               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
10032               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
10033               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
10034               	; 	' before any of this.
10035               	; 	'
10036               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
10037               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
10038               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
10039               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his
10040               	; 	' journey.
10041               	; 	'
10042               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels
10043               	; 	' travelled, not time -- so the run cycle stays locked to the ground at any
10044               	; 	' rate. A 9 px step moves it exactly one pose of its 8 px beat.

10505               	;
10506               	; 	' ======================================================================
10507               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10508               	; 	' ======================================================================
10509               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10510               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10511               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10512               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10513               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10514               	; 	'
10515               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10516               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10517               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10518               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10519               	; 	' broken.
10520               	; 	'
10521               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10522               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10523               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10524               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10525               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10526               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10527               	; 	'
10528               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10529               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10530               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10531               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10532               	; coll_obst:
10533               cvb_COLL_OBST
10534               	; 	IF klst = ST_ESC THEN RETURN		' riding is invincible, per the
10535 DF36 D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLST,r0
     DF38 21C2     
10536 DF3A 0201  20 	li r1,768   ; 3*256
     DF3C 0300     
10537 DF3E 9001  18 	cb r1,r0
10538 DF40 1302  14 	jeq cv657
10539 DF42 0460  28 	b @cv656
     DF44 DF4A     
10540               cv657
10541 DF46 C03A  30 	mov *r10+,r0
10542 DF48 0450  20 	b *r0
10543               cv656
10544               	; 	IF klst = ST_ELEV THEN RETURN		' manual: "until you step out"
10545 DF4A D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLST,r0
     DF4C 21C2     
10546 DF4E 0201  20 	li r1,1024   ; 4*256
     DF50 0400     
10547 DF52 9001  18 	cb r1,r0

10893               	; 	' ONE PASS LONGER THAN THE SOUND, because the sound does not start here.
10894               	; 	' sfh is a latch that sfx_tick consumes on the NEXT pass, so the note
10895               	; 	' runs passes 2..HITSND+1 of the freeze and this ends with it.

     E1F0 1500     
10898 E1F2 D800  38 	movb r0,@cvb_HFZ
     E1F4 21A0     
10899               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10900               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10901               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10902               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10903               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10904               	; 	' away from.
10905               	; 	'
10906               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10907               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10908               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10909               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10910               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10911               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10912               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10913               	; 	'
10914               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10915               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10916               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and

11088               	; 	' AND THEY HAVE TO BE AT THE SAME HEIGHT, NOT MERELY ON THE SAME FLOOR.
11089               	; 	'
11090               	; 	' `hlv` does not change until a ride ENDS -- a crook stepping onto a
11091               	; 	' flight keeps the floor he left until he arrives at the next one. So
11092               	; 	' while he was most of a storey up or down the stairs he still counted as
11093               	; 	' standing on the floor he started from, and a Kop who ran over the head
11094               	; 	' of the flight arrested him through the floor. Reported from play:
11095               	; 	' "I run over top of him, even though we do not touch".
11096               	; 	'
11097               	; 	' It is the same shape of bug as the catch that fired at MAXIMUM
11098               	; 	' separation: a test that is right about one axis and silent about the
11099               	; 	' other, where the silent one happens to be true nearly all the time.
11100               	; 	'
11101               	; 	' UNSIGNED-SAFE. Riding up is above the shared floor and riding down is
11102               	; 	' below it, which is a signed quantity, and CVBasic's variables are not.
11103               	; 	' So both are collected as POSITIVE heights on opposite sides -- Kelly's
11104               	; 	' climb plus Harry's descent on one side, Harry's climb on the other --
11105               	; 	' and the difference is taken between two numbers that cannot go
11106               	; 	' negative. Two riders passing on the same flight measure the sum of
11107               	; 	' their heights, which is exactly the distance between them.

11213               	; 	' RIDING WITH THE DOORS SHUT: HIDE HIM AND DO NOT DRAW HIM AT ALL.
11214               	; 	'

11216               	; 	' placed him at his old floor and then hid him again. That is not free.
11217               	; 	' CVBasic's SPRITE writes a RAM mirror which the vblank ISR copies to
11218               	; 	' VRAM, so a vblank landing BETWEEN the draw and the hide latches the
11219               	; 	' visible state for a frame -- and draw_actors is long (Kelly, Harry,
11220               	; 	' eight obstacles) while a pass on the lift screen spans two or three
11221               	; 	' frames, so it happened constantly. He flickered at the floor he had
11222               	; 	' just left, which reads as a drawing bug rather than as a journey.
11223               	; 	'

11814               	; 	' half, so both boxes span rows 0-15 and neither can be tucked away --

11819               	; 	' HE RISES A PIXEL ON THE RECOVERY BEATS. A runner is highest at mid-flight
11820               	; 	' and lowest at contact; with the body pinned at a constant y, alternating
11821               	; 	' legs under a motionless torso reads as a dance rather than as travel.
11822               	; 	'
11823               	; 	' One pixel is enough at this size, and it lifts the BODY ONLY -- the legs
11824               	; 	' keep their y, so the planted foot stays on the floor and the figure
11825               	; 	' stretches at the waist instead of hopping. Lifting the legs too would be
11826               	; 	' a jump.

11828               	; 	' Beats 2 and 4 are the recoveries, which is exactly `hanim AND 8` -- the
11829               	; 	' cycle's LOW beat bit. IT MUST MOVE WITH THE BEAT BITS ABOVE IT: on the
11830               	; 	' wrong bit he rises and falls twice per stride, a second clock inside one
11831               	; 	' figure, which is the flapping of DESIGN.md 0j2 in the vertical.
11832               	; 	'

12295               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
12296               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
12297               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
12298               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
12299               	; 	'
12300               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
12301               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
12302               	; 	'
12303               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
12304               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
12305               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
12306               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
12307               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
12308               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
12309               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
12310               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
12311               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
12312               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
12313               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
12314               	; esc_tick:
12315               cvb_ESC_TICK
12316               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
12317               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
12318               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
12319               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).

12339               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
12340               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
12341               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
12342               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
12343               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
12344               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
12345               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
12346               	; 	'
12347               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
12348               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
12349               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
12350               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
12351               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
12352               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
12353               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.

12650               	;
12651               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12652               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12653               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12654               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12655               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12656               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12657               	; 	'
12658               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12659               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12660               	; 	' exactly one colour here:

13036               	; 	' Blank the canvas by WRITING zeros rather than copying 384 of them out
13037               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
13038               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
13039               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
13040               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
13041               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).
13042               	; scan_wipe:

13044               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
13045               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
13046               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
13047               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
13048               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
13049               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
13050               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
13051               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
13052               	; 	'
13053               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
13054               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
13055               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
13056               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
13057               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
13058               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
13059               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
13060               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
13061               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
13062               	; 	'
13063               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
13064               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
13065               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
13066               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
13067               	; 	'

13961               	;
13962               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13963               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13964               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13965               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13966               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13967               	; 	'
13968               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13969               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13970               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13971               	; 	'
13972               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13973               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13974               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13975               	; 	'
13976               	; 	' IN UNITS OF TEN, WHICH IS WHAT THE SCORE IS COUNTED IN, so the bands are
13977               	; 	' 10 / 20 / 30 and not 100 / 200 / 300.
13978               	; 	'
13979               	; 	' They were 100 / 200 / 300 and paid TEN TIMES the right bonus -- 1,000 a
13980               	; 	' time unit where the original pays 100. `add_score` takes `#addv` in units
13981               	; 	' of ten (the prize beside it is `#addv = 5` for fifty points, and the bonus
13982               	; 	' Kop threshold is `#nextk = 1000` for ten thousand), so writing the band in
13983               	; 	' POINTS here shifted every tally one decimal place. Reported from play as
13984               	; 	' "it seems like you awarded 1000 per time unit left" -- exactly right.
13985               	; 	'
13986               	; 	' Nothing failed: 1,000 a unit is a plausible-looking number, the digits
13987               	; 	' all line up, and the only symptom is a score that runs away. The tell is
13988               	; 	' a constant written in a different unit from the routine it is passed to,
13989               	; 	' which is the same class of fault as the px-per-pass speeds in 3A.
13990               	; 	'
13991               	; 	' (This is also why the old comment here said "#bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300
13992               	; 	' does not fit in a byte". At 10 / 20 / 30 it would, but it stays 16-bit
13993               	; 	' because `#addv` is, and a byte here would buy two bytes of ROM in
13994               	; 	' exchange for a truncation trap the next time somebody edits a band.)

14111               	;
14112               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
14113               	; 	'
14114               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
14115               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
14116               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
14117               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
14118               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
14119               	; 	'
14120               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
14121               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
14122               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
14123               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
14124               	; 	' counting stops.

14437               	;
14438               	; 	' A SOUND STILL PLAYING WHEN THE ROUND ENDS IS ALLOWED TO FINISH.
14439               	; 	'
14440               	; 	' This used to open with a bare `GOSUB snd_off`, which cut it dead. That
14441               	; 	' was not an accident: the decay counters are ticked by the MAIN LOOP, and
14442               	; 	' this pause REPLACES the main loop, so a tone left latched with nothing
14443               	; 	' ticking it hangs for the full ninety frames -- the sticky-audio failure
14444               	; 	' this game has already shipped twice. The answer is to DRAIN the counters
14445               	; 	' rather than to stop silencing.
14446               	; 	'
14447               	; 	' CLEAR THE PENDING LATCHES FIRST. sf* flags are sounds that have not
14448               	; 	' happened yet; left set, the drain below would START one and the pause
14449               	; 	' would end with a fresh note ringing into the next round.
14450               	; 	'
14451               	; 	' THEN TICK sfx_tick WHOLE, not some decay-only part of it. The five
14452               	; 	' counters do not all live in one place: sot, sht and spt are a block at
14453               	; 	' the tail, but spz (the prize arpeggio) and swt (the jump warble) tick up
14454               	; 	' among the code that starts sounds. Draining only the tail would finish a
14455               	; 	' footstep and still cut the arpeggio, which is the one effect with a
14456               	; 	' phrase worth saving. Calling the whole routine also leaves the write
14457               	; 	' order on CHANNEL 2 alone, which spz and spt share.
14458               	; 	'
14459               	; 	' EVERY THIRD FRAME, because the main loop runs about 2.5 frames per pass
14460               	; 	' and this loop waits one frame per turn. Ticking every frame would play
14461               	; 	' everything at two and a half times its tuned speed. Three frames a tick
14462               	; 	' is ~17% slow and gives 30 ticks against the longest effect's 20 passes.
14463               	; 	'
14464               	; 	' THE LOOP COUNTS TICKS, NOT FRAMES, which is what makes the pacing free.
14465               	; 	' Counting 91 frames and firing on every third needs a second counter, an
14466               	; 	' increment and a test -- 48 bytes, on a fixed area with 66 left. Counting
14467               	; 	' 31 TICKS of three WAITs each is the same 93 frames and the same three
14468               	; 	' frames per tick, with none of that. The duration changes by two frames.
14469               	; 	'
14470               	; 	' snd_off still runs at the END, as the backstop for anything the drain
14471               	; 	' did not finish.
14472               	; pause_beat:
14473               cvb_PAUSE_BEAT

14835               	;
14836               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14837               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14838               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14839               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14840               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14841               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14842               	;
14843               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14844               	; 	'
14845               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14846               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14847               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14848               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14849               	; 	'
14850               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14851               	; 	'
14852               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14853               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14854               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14855               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14856               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14857               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14858               	; 	'
14859               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14860               	; 	'
14861               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14862               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14863               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14864               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14865               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14866               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14867               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14868               	; 	'
14869               	; 	' MEASURED OFF THE COLECOVISION: 14 px, about 7.4 a second.
14870               	; 	'
14871               	; 	' It was 15 px and 6.9 a second, picked between an 8.0 that read as
14872               	; 	' slightly hurried and a 6.1 that read as trudging -- a judgement between
14873               	; 	' two other judgements, with nothing underneath it. The ColecoVision
14874               	; 	' recording settles it: footfalls land every 0.130 s across a twelve-second
14875               	; 	' continuous run, which is 7.7 a second, and that is the one finding in the
14876               	; 	' whole sound analysis the method resolves EXACTLY -- a rhythm rather than a
14877               	; 	' pitch, counted off the RMS track rather than inferred from a spectrum.
14878               	; 	' (colecosounds variant 1A; assets/sfx/sfxref-coleco.md has the working.)
14879               	; 	'
14880               	; 	' 104 px/s over 14 px is 7.43 a second. 13 px would give 8.00, and 7.7 sits
14881               	; 	' almost exactly between them -- so this is the nearer of the two, and it is
14882               	; 	' also the one that does not walk back into the 8.0 that was rejected by ear.
14883               	; 	'
14884               	; 	' WHY THE GAME KEEPS A DISTANCE AND THE BENCH KEEPS A CADENCE. The bench
14885               	; 	' plays a fixed eight frames between steps because it has no walking to tie
14886               	; 	' them to; the game accumulates PIXELS TRAVELLED, so the feet keep time with
14887               	; 	' the legs when he is slowed or stopped. Matching "7.4 a second" therefore
14888               	; 	' means matching it AT HIS WALKING SPEED, and assumes the ColecoVision's
14889               	; 	' crook walks at ours -- which the recording cannot confirm.
14890               	; 	'
14891               	; 	' The dial is this one constant and the subtraction below, which must stay
14892               	; 	' threshold + 1 or the carry is wrong.
14893               	; 	'
14894               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14895               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14896               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14897               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14898               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14899               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14900               	; 	'
14901               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14902               	; 	'
14903               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14904               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14905               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14906               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14907               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14908               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
14909               	; 	' back to 7.
14910               	; 	IF sfw > 13 THEN

15108               	;
15109               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
15110               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
15111               	; 	'
15112               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
15113               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
15114               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
15115               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
15116               	; 	'
15117               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
15118               	; 	'
15119               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
15120               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
15121               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
15122               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
15123               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
15124               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
15125               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
15126               	; 	'
15127               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
15128               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
15129               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
15130               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
15131               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
15132               	; 	'
15133               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
15134               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
15135               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
15136               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
15137               	; 	#if TI994A
15138               	; 	BANK 2
15139      0184     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$

15803               	; 	INCLUDE "art.bas"
15804               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15805               	; 	'
15806               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15807               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15808               	; 	' being small sprites.
15809               	; 	'
15810               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15811               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15812               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15813               	; 	'
15814               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15815               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15816               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15817               	;
15818               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15819               cvb_SPR_KELLY

16932               	;
16933               	; 	' -------------------------------------------------- scanner canvas
16934               	; 	' Chars 208-255: 16 cols x 3 rows over screen rows 21-23. Blank to start;
16935               	; 	' dots are plotted by VPOKEing the PATTERN table (rows 21-23 sit in the
16936               	; 	' third screen third, so every scanner pattern is at base 4096).
16937               	;
16938               	; 	' --------------------------------------------------- font colours
16939               	; 	' Chars 32-90, EIGHT bytes each. Without this the font keeps whatever
16940               	; 	' CVBasic left in the colour table, which on a green store made the HUD
16941               	; 	' unreadable.
16942               	;
16943               	; scan_col3:	' one 8-byte block per canvas row: 4 px of GREY margin, then a 3 px band of furniture GREY and a yellow floor line, per 4 px level, on dark green. The Kop and the crook are coloured PER CHARACTER at run time -- see scan_set
16944               cvb_SCAN_COL3

17059               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
17060               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
17061               	; 	'
17062               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
17063               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
17064               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
17065               	; 	'
17066               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
17067               	; 	' blit is
17068               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
17069               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
17070               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
17071               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
17072               	; 	'
17073               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
17074               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
17075               	; 	'
17076               	; 	' template ids:
17077               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
17078               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
17079               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
17080               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
17081               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
17082               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
17083               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
17084               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
17085               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
17086               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
17087               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
17088               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
17089               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
17090               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
17091               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
17092               	;
17093               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
17094               cvb_STOR_TPL
